problems.title: ⭐ No 7-Day AI Team Handling Inbound Enquiries, Booking, Follow-Up, Payments, and Client Updates
problems.description: Martine was told we can build a 7-day free trial AI team that works across every department — but today there is no unified system doing that. New enquiries still depend on the owner being available. Bookings require manual back-and-forth. Leads who asked questions but never booked go cold. Outstanding invoices are not chased consistently. Clients waiting on reports or next steps are forced to call in for updates. For a niche built on trust, urgency, and reassurance, that means revenue leakage at every stage of the client journey.
problems.impact: Lost bookings, slower cash collection, and anxious clients across the full pipeline — from first inquiry to final payment
problems.evidence: Owner-operator workflow + multi-step inspection/report/remediation cycle creates obvious automation opportunities across intake, follow-up, payments, and updates

problems.title: After-Hours Inquiries Going Unanswered
problems.description: Health anxiety doesn't follow business hours. A parent Googling 'mold inspector Nashville' at 10pm after seeing black spots near the baby's room is a high-intent, emotionally ready buyer. As a small owner-operator business, there's no staff to respond until the next morning — by which time the prospect has already booked with whoever responded first. The owner-inspector is often in the field during business hours too, creating the same gap during peak calling windows.
problems.impact: Estimated 20–30% of web inquiries arrive outside business hours — most book with the first responder
problems.evidence: Owner-operator model with no after-hours coverage; field schedule during core business hours creates double exposure

problems.title: Leads, Payments, and Client Updates Still Depend on Manual Chasing
problems.description: Once an inquiry comes in, the follow-through is still manual. Prospects who asked questions but did not book are easy to lose. Open invoices depend on someone remembering to follow up. Clients waiting on lab results, reports, or next steps often call in because there is no proactive update sequence. That creates avoidable admin load and a weaker client experience.
problems.impact: Warm leads cool off, cash collection slows down, and clients feel uncertain while waiting for answers
problems.evidence: Owner-operator workflow + report delivery cycle means follow-up, payment reminders, and status updates are easy to delay without automation

problems.title: Google Reviews Not Keeping Pace with Completed Jobs
problems.description: Indoor Environmental Testing has 20+ years of experience and hundreds of satisfied families — but that track record isn't fully visible on Google. Every job ends with a grateful homeowner who finally has answers after months of unexplained symptoms. Those are perfect review moments. But without a systematic ask at the right time (24–48 hours after the report lands, when relief is highest), most clients never think to leave a review. Meanwhile, newer competitors with fewer qualifications are building larger review counts simply because they ask every single time. In a niche where trust is everything and families are scared, Google reviews are a strong secondary growth lever.
problems.impact: Review growth is slower than it should be, reducing visibility in local search over time
problems.evidence: High satisfaction implied by referral volume, but review count lags behind service output

problems.title: Referral Partners Not Systematically Nurtured
problems.description: Real estate agents, pediatricians, allergists, and remediation contractors are the highest-value referral sources in this niche — one active realtor partner can send 15–20 inspections per year. But referral relationships die from neglect. Without a system sending monthly educational content, referral thank-yous, and outcome updates to partners, the referral channel is entirely dependent on personal relationships that fade over time.
problems.impact: Referral channel producing far below potential — untapped 2–3x growth opportunity
problems.evidence: Dual-market operation (Nashville + Madison) requires scalable partner outreach — can't rely on in-person relationship maintenance

problems.title: Seasonal Demand Spikes Not Being Capitalized On
problems.description: Nashville and Madison both have distinct mold and air quality seasons — spring humidity in Tennessee, fall basement moisture in Wisconsin, HVAC startup season (when contaminated ducts distribute spores), and wildfire smoke events. These are high-intent windows when homeowners are primed to act. Without automated seasonal campaigns to past clients and referral partners, this demand spike goes to whoever has visibility at the right moment.
problems.impact: Peak season demand not pre-captured — reactive rather than proactive scheduling
problems.evidence: Dual-market operation spans two distinct climate zones with different seasonal patterns
